finalText:
Both let you combine work from two branches, but they get there differently.

**Merge** keeps history as it happened. It adds a new commit that ties the two branches together, so you can see exactly when and how they joined. Nothing gets rewritten. It's the safe pick for shared branches — anything other people have already pulled — because you're not changing commits that already exist.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the other branch, one by one, as if you'd written them there from the start. History ends up as one clean, straight line with no merge commit. The catch: it rewrites commit history, so it's risky on a branch anyone else is using. Fine on your own local, not-yet-shared branch.

Rule of thumb: rebase your own feature branch to keep it tidy before you share it. Once it's shared, merge from then on.
